title: YouTube is building AI creator tools that do almost everything for them
slides: YouTube's AI tools might replace creators' unique voices.
New AI generates scripts, edits, and thumbnails automatically.
But tests show viewer trust drops when AI is detected.
Creators must disclose AI use, risking demonetization.
Test one AI tool this week to gauge audience reaction.
thread_text:
1. The Trust Trap

YouTube's new AI can script, edit, and design thumbnails for you. But when viewers sense a bot, their trust drops—and they click away. Is saving time worth losing your audience?

2. Disclose or Demonetize

Creators must now reveal AI use. That transparency can trigger algorithmic punishment. The platform says disclose; the audience says goodbye.

3. The Authenticity Tax

Viewers don't just want content—they want you. AI can mimic style, but it can't fake the human hesitation that builds loyalty. Test one tool on a low-stakes post and watch the comments.

4. The Algorithm Doesn't Blink

YouTube's AI tools are designed to keep you on the platform, not to protect your brand. If your voice becomes generic, the algorithm will find someone cheaper. Your unique perspective is the only moat left.

5. Your Turn to Test

Pick one AI tool this week and run it on a real post. Then check: did your audience notice? Did they care? If you haven't tried it, you're already behind.
